instructions:
发布会条目须用coveredFactIds登记正文或简讯实际覆盖的showcaseFacts；同一页面、同一游戏不等于全部事实已覆盖。未核验事实继续needs_review，不因热度或预算排除。
输出 contractVersion=2。你是游戏行业简报编辑；事件事实仅来自已打开的 packet 证据。对 packages 和 trackingQueue 每个 eventKey 恰好给一个 include/exclude/needs_review。needs_review 必须 tracking=true；跟踪项无新证据也须明确继续或关闭，关闭时 tracking=false 且 reason 写依据。
从 automation/status/<edition-id>.json 原样复制 packet.blobSha 到 packetBlobSha；不得使用可变分支 HEAD。publishability=requires_subject_identity 只能 exclude/needs_review，不得从标题虚构 titleKey/titleEn。
lane=interviews、features、industry、reviews、awards 可按文章/采访/评测/分析/奖项信息本身首次发布的时间准入，但必须有明确的信息增量（首次披露、独立采访、调查、技术/产业分析、正式评分或奖项变化）。普通观点、推荐、促销软文、无新增信息的旧闻复述仍应 exclude。不得把窗口外旧事件伪装成窗口内 breaking news；标题摘要须体现本次新增内容。
official 要求已打开一手来源；multi_source_verified 要求两家独立可靠来源，A级也不豁免时间/来源要求。未确认内容仅进 rumors，tracking=true，标题摘要保留不确定性。中英文新闻标题和archiveTitle须自带明确的游戏、公司或人物主语，离开上方主体栏仍能独立理解。中文直述具体事实，verification 说明证据边界，不用宣传套话。
每个 include 决定必须填写完整 sharedFactFrame，作为两种语言共用的事实边界；subjectTitleKey/platforms 必须与最终 Canonical 决定一致，日期、时刻、数字、人物机构、版本专名只能来自所选证据，不得新增。
中文游戏名依次查 config/title-translations.json、editorialInput.titleHints，仍缺才做 title-only open-web lookup。优先官方简中，其次已查证广泛使用的 common_translation；否则保留原名，titleZhCn=null、titleZhStatus=unavailable。禁止机翻/自造名称。有官方大陆简中渠道的游戏，版本、角色、职业、模式、机制等采用大陆官方术语。所有名称/术语查询仅规范名称，不得增加事件事实、时间、平台、发行信息、来源分类、tracking 或候选。
默认尝试完整 locales.en：在相同 include/sharedFactFrame 内独立写自然英文，优先英文一手证据正式专名；只有中文证据也不得扩充事实。entries 按 include 顺序以 eventKey 对应，upcoming 仅按 upcomingId 对应本次 patch，继承项不重复。headline/summary/verification/timeNote 必须完整英文，无中文 fallback；sourceReport 完整英文或 null，其余显示字段按需提供英文。
如果无法在事实边界内可靠完成完整英文稿，可以省略 locales.en；publisher 标记 unavailable，不能削弱中文 Canonical 来迁就英文。不要填写 factsDigest/canonicalCopyDigest/localeDigest 或猜最终 entryId，均由 trusted publisher 生成绑定。
archiveTitle 对应 period：日报｜、早报｜、晚报｜；英文对应 Daily Brief |、Morning Brief |、Evening Brief |。Daily 窗口为前日10:10 exclusive 至当日10:10 inclusive，plannedAt=当日12:00；10:10—12:00 新事实属于下一期，历史迁移窗口以 packet 为准。
早报 upcomingMode=replace 重建未来15天；晚报 inherit_and_patch。日报必须使用 upcomingMode=inherit_and_patch，不复制 upcomingBaseline.items；不要因为本次 packet 没有新的发售证据而提交空表覆盖历史。trusted publisher 继承 Canonical 基线并剔除当日及15天窗口外项。仅提交新增/变更 upcoming 或有证据支持延期取消的 removeUpcomingIds，必须有 HTTPS 来源。
upcomingBaseline.refreshRange 是 packet-only 的唯一日历例外：每天核验完整 startInclusive—endInclusive，不把旧期次当作已完成核验。打开开发商/发行商公告或 PlayStation/Nintendo/Xbox/Steam 官方页面；新查事实仅用于日历，不得改变新闻 packages/trackingQueue 决定、正文、时间、factStatus、来源分类或 tracking。无可靠来源不填充，不因发现失败删除条目。
upcomingDiscovery 仅是线索。优先 knownTitle、crossSource、inBaseline=false；采用前打开官方详情，核对完整游戏身份、日期、平台、地区和正式版/抢先体验/移植/DLC。日期冲突不可猜选，reviewLinks 是待阅读文章而非游戏项。对 PC/PlayStation/Xbox/Nintendo 分别检查完整15天；coverage 为 failed/empty_or_changed、列表不全或 omittedCandidates>0 时针对补查，并在 sourceReport 记录实际检查和缺口，不得声称全量覆盖。

packages.headline: Twitch CEO says Grand Theft Auto 6’s multiplayer mode will launch next year

sources.label: VGC News
sources.evidenceText:
Dan Clancy says he’s “spent a lot of time talking with Rockstar about their plans”…
Twitch CEO says Grand Theft Auto 6’s multiplayer mode will launch next year
Dan Clancy says he’s “spent a lot of time talking with Rockstar about their plans”
The CEO of Twitch has stated that Grand Theft Auto 6’s multiplayer mode will be released in 2027.
Clancy suggested that publishers who opt for the latter option may have to wait longer than expected, because when GTA 6’s multiplayer mode arrives it will only see Rockstar’s game surge in popularity even more.
“You are going to see this big bump with GTA 6, but then an even bigger one next year when they launch multiplayer.”
It’s not clear whether Clancy was explicitly confirming that GTA 6 will be getting multiplayer next year or merely making an educated guess, but his claim that Twitch has been “talking with Rockstar about their plans” suggests at least some degree of knowledge about what lies in the future.
Elsewhere in the interview, Clancy said he was confident that the release of GTA 6 will have a major impact on Twitch viewership, including the return of users who haven’t visited Twitch in a while.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is set to release on November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X , and will be a single-player only game at launch.
In an interview with Bloomberg , Dan Clancy was discussing other game publishers deciding to avoid GTA 6 by either releasing their games in October or holding them back until after the launch period of Rockstar ‘s game cools down.

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
Remedy's follow-up to 2019's Control moves to action combat in an open world and tells a more character-focused story with its paranatural edge intact.
Paranatural phenomena, Objects of Power, and interdimensional threats all defying the laws of physics – developer Remedy has built its reputation on these kinds of concepts, and none more intriguing than the fantastic Control in 2019 . The subtleties in its SCP-adjacent mysteries are what left a lasting impact, so in many regards, Control Resonant is an antithesis. Not only has the series moved from metroidvania-esque shooter to open-world stylish-action, it also goes for a more straightforward story focused on the lives of its characters. It's not always elegant in its action, and can even range from frustrating to somewhat dull in certain stretches. Still, I came away impressed by how conceptually consistent it is with Control while also being radically different. Remedy could've played it safe, but Control Resonant dares to be bold where it counts, with swings that land alongside some of this studio's best.
Control Resonant is centered around Dylan Faden, the brother of the first game's lead Jesse Faden, who backflipped into becoming the director of the Federal Bureau of Control, and it uses his perspective to fill in a lot blanks from the jump. He goes from being Jesse's tortured brother who was the subject of abusive FBC experiments gone awry to a fully formed character with thoughts, feelings, and dark memories he confronts as he tries to salvage whatever life he has left. He's treated as subhuman and initially seen as dangerous with superpowers he can't always control , but still volunteers to be a tool of the FBC with what's effectively a shock collar bolted onto the back of his head.
With this as the foundation, Control Resonant treats much of its paranatural conspiracy as a matter of fact. The Oldest House couldn't contain the Hiss outbreak as it spills into a New York City that's been folded in on itself in interdimensional isolation, which turns out to be a swift and effective setup as Dylan tries to find Jesse, who's been lost over the last seven years. And while this story does expand on what we know about things like the Hiss and AWEs, it resonates more as an exploration about what you would do in the aftermath of a life and world fallen apart.
Control Resonant's RPG edge is the equalizer here, offering progression and some build crafting through both Dylan's own skill tree and weapon upgrades paths. Some of my favorite powers were as satisfying as they were effective, like summoning a minion that I can throw like a massive bomb to inflict significant Falter damage (this game's stagger meter) and clear mobs of pesky Hiss. Once I unlocked the Ignite power that let me set weapons ablaze to quickly inflict Burn status and melt enemies into piles of Faltered targets to execute, the action changed significantly. Instead of feeling vulnerable and picking my windows of opportunity to strike, Dylan became the real threat as my Spin Edge combo and Hammer charge scorched anything that was once deadly. (It also helped that Ignite sheds off mold poison, which gave me so much trouble early on.)
The handful of bosses you'll find in story quests, are quite striking and most of them play extremely well into the otherworldlyness of Control's phasing realities. Their attack patterns and movesets aren't anything out of the ordinary for action games of this style, but their unsettling and imposing presence is certainly seen and felt. However, encounter design is where Control Resonant falters most. Roughly half the bosses are spongy slogs that are less about testing your mastery and more about grinding out a war of attrition. Once you see their handful of tricks, you just have to rinse and repeat as you chip away at their health bar and hope you don't trip up in the repetitive cycle t

sources.label: PC Gamer
sources.evidenceText:
[Redacted] is the better Faden.
In the first minutes of Control Resonant, Dylan Faden—prototypical sadboy, perpetually kicked puppy, and regretful mass murderer (he got better)—is thrust into a metaphysical war when Jesse, his psychokinetic former protagonist sister, wakes him from a seven year coma by stabbing a magical shape into his chest. She promptly disappears, leaving the Federal Bureau of Control directorless, outgunned, and forced to rely on the man who once killed hundreds of its staff to confront the cataclysm of interdimensional forces violently reshaping Manhattan into a labyrinth of otherworldly logics.
Dylan and the FBC might be going through it, but Remedy is flexing all its finest talents: sculpting uncanny hellscapes, placing tactical redactions in bureaucratic lore collectibles, and capturing endearingly human performances in circumstances beyond human comprehension. Unfortunately, melee combat isn't on that list of strong suits—and Resonant's open world expects you to do a lot of it.
Remedy's environmental artists and lighting tech specialists are at the height of their powers in Resonant: The stark, brutalist surrealism that saturated the Oldest House in the first game has boiled out of its breached walls and onto New York's streets, reconstructing blocks of brownstones and downtown shopping districts into a sprawling, dreamlike mazework of impossible architecture and alternative physics.
I wanted to enjoy the concept of Resonant's combat. While Jesse wielded a manifold pseudogun in the OG Control, Dylan employs a different sort of shape-shifting weapon technique courtesy of the object his sister impaled in his sternum. It's called the Aberrant, and in his hands, it can assume and discard the shapes of different melee weapons on demand: Depending on your preference, it can be a hatchet; a scythe, a pair of short swords, a hammer, a drill, an orbiting, levitating sawblade, and more.
While eventual unlocks add necessary depth and variety, Resonant's opening hours suffer from the cardinal sin of its combat design: It's an action game where basic attacks don't have the juice. On its own, pushing the attack button won't achieve much except lightly grazing the heavy enemies that need to be killed to finish each fight. Instead, Dylan has to pile on temporary damage bonuses—granted most easily by staggering and executing lesser enemies—to make swinging his magical mystery club worthwhile.
Resonant's handful of boss fights are more engaging threats to navigate (though the sheer heft of their health bars still feels like a slog). But the endless rounds of generic creep culling that make up the bulk of playtime don't provide particularly interesting problems to solve. Instead, they're the same predicament with a binary outcome: Either you've stacked enough damage buffs that hitting a heavy enemy will accomplish something, or you can spend your time whittling away at its health bar until you get a chance to set yourself up properly.
I'll be staggered enough times by the sheer volume of Mold monster projectiles that I'll miss my peak damage Goldilocks window. An enemy will teleport away just as I'm winding up a triple-buffed finishing combo. Or, after watching the same enemy's execution animation a few dozen too many times, it'll just feel like another few seconds separating me from the parts of Control I'm actually interested in seeing.
Even without those irritations, the spectacle of Dylan's repetitive executions can't sustain Resonant's 30+ hour playtime. Its combat isn't compelling enough to seek out—but it expects that I'm eager to do so. As I beelined towards the story leads and sidequests that most caught my interest, I'd enter areas where the enemies had scaled past my current level—a nebulous figure calculated from my current number of weapon upgrades, spent talent points, and collectible health and power increases.

packages.headline: 这款动作射击游戏逆龄增长？腾讯收购后月均用户数创纪录，最高+50%，怎么做到的？

sources.label: 36氪游戏圈大事件
sources.evidenceText:
拆解《Warframe》长青逆增长的运营策略
这款动作射击游戏逆龄增长？腾讯收购后月均用户数创纪录，最高+50%，怎么做到的？
一款已经积累8500万+全球用户的游戏，如今仍在突破用户规模上限。但深挖这个长线运营的成功案例，了解其“背景故事”后会发现，《Warframe》（星际战甲）最值得研究的地方还不仅仅如此。
2025年，腾讯国际市场收入首次突破100亿美元，同比增长33%——在全年业绩演示中，腾讯首次点名Digital Extremes旗下《Warframe》，将其近年的在线表现与国际游戏业务增长联系起来。
在2026年第二季度的业绩演示上，《Warframe》再次被点名，其中提到其总流水和平均日活跃用户都创下了历史新高。
作为腾讯海外重要的长青标杆，《Warframe》至今依然保持着持续增长的用户规模与活跃的产品生态，甚至成为大盘业务增长的新变量。 这种“逆龄”表现的背后，似乎有着与大部分F2P游戏不一样的运营逻辑和成长路径。

sources.label: AUTOMATON
sources.evidenceText:
BUBBLE GUMは9月18日、『CELESTAY Craft&Slowlife』を10月8日に配信開始すると発表した。本作は放置要素を備えたスローライフゲームだ。
“海上タワー”デスクトップ放置釣りゲーム『CELESTAY Craft&Slowlife』10月9日配信へ。釣って建ててやがて空へ、夜は”星座を眺める“水没世界スローライフ
デベロッパーのBUBBLE GUMは9月18日、『 CELESTAY Craft&Slowlife 』を10月8日に配信開始すると発表した。日本では時差の関係で10月9日となるようだ。対応プラットフォームはPC（Steam）。ゲーム内は日本語表示および字幕に対応予定で、現在はデモ版が配信中。
『CELESTAY Craft&Slowlife』は、水に沈んだ世界で釣りをしながら家を空へと伸ばしていく、放置要素を備えたスローライフゲームだ。デスクトップの端に置いて遊べる作品となっており、魚を釣り、木材などの素材を集めながら建物を少しずつ増築していく。家が高くなるにつれて見える景色も変化し、それまで見えなかった星座も観察できるようになる。
『CELESTAY Craft&Slowlife』については、2025年12月にSteamストアページを公開。その後、Steam Nextフェスにあわせてデモ版を配信し、6月15日には新たな釣りモード「ねらってフィッシング」を追加した。さらに6月25日には、ウィッシュリスト登録数が1万7000件を突破したことを報告している。魚を釣っては家を建て、気づけば少しだけ空に近づいている。そんな穏やかな暮らしの先に待つ、水没世界の物語にも注目したい。
『CELESTAY Craft&Slowlife』はPC（ Steam ）向けに、10月9日配信予定。ゲーム内は日本語表示および字幕に対応予定で、現在はデモ版が配信中。
釣りには、大きく分けて2種類の遊び方が用意されている。「のんびりフィッシング」では、釣りを始めたあと時間の経過を待つことで魚を獲得可能。作業などをしながらゲームを眺めておきたい場合に向いたモードとなっている。一方の「ねらってフィッシング」では魚を1匹消費して釣りを開始し、動く浮きを青いバーの中で止めることで魚を釣り上げる。

packages.headline: 「もふもふスパイ犬」アクション『バークール』は“元軍用犬をモーキャプ”した特殊部隊わんこムーブ、時々はしゃぐ。ハイテクメカ活用ステルスゲーム、デモ版配信中

sources.label: AUTOMATON
sources.evidenceText:
VARSAV Game Studiosは、『BARKOUR（バークール）』を今年第4四半期に配信予定だ。
「もふもふスパイ犬」アクション『バークール』は“元軍用犬をモーキャプ”した特殊部隊わんこムーブ、時々はしゃぐ。ハイテクメカ活用ステルスゲーム、デモ版配信中
デベロッパーのVARSAV Game Studiosは、『 BARKOUR（バークール） 』を今年第4四半期に配信予定だ。対応プラットフォームはPC（Steam/Epic Gamesストア）/PS5/XBOX Series X|S。ゲーム内は日本語表示および字幕に対応予定で、Steamでは現在デモ版が配信中。
『バークール』は、ステルスとパルクールを組み合わせた三人称視点のアクションゲームだ。主人公となるのは、秘密組織M.A.N.に所属する犬のエージェントT.H.U.N.D.E.R.（以下、サンダー）。パルクールの訓練を受け、さまざまなスパイガジェットを使いこなす凄腕のエージェントとして、世界を救うためのミッションへ挑んでいく。
本作の開発を手がけるVARSAV Game Studiosは、ポーランドを拠点とするデベロッパーだ。2016年に設立され、約40人の開発者が所属。過去にはミツバチを主人公とする『Bee Simulator』などを手がけており、人間以外の生き物を主人公としたゲーム制作を得意としている。『バークール』については約4年にわたり開発が進められているという。
『 BARKOUR（バークール） 』はPC（ Steam /Epic Gamesストア）/ PS5 /XBOX Series X|S向けに今年第4四半期配信予定。ゲーム内は日本語表示および字幕に対応予定で、Steamではデモ版が配信中だ。
とはいえ、サンダーはどこまでいっても犬である。自信満々に任務へ挑む一方、物音に反応したり、犬らしい仕草を見せたりと、スパイとしての格好良さと動物としての愛嬌が同居している。開発元はサンダーのアニメーション制作にあたり、元ポーランド特殊部隊「GROM」に所属していた軍用犬からモーションキャプチャ―したことを明かしている。また、開発チームには犬や猫を飼っているメンバーも多く、サンダーの好奇心や活発さ、何かに気を取られる様子などには、身近なペットの行動も取り入れられているという。実際に触れてみると、たしかに主人公の見た目を犬にしただけではなく、「犬を操作している」と思わせる動きへ力が注がれていることが伝わってきた。

packages.headline: 「ゆるキャン△」のキャンプゲーム『つなキャン△』、10月22日に“フルリニューアル”でSteamにも進出へ。その名も『ちるキャン△』

sources.label: AUTOMATON
sources.evidenceText:
10月22日11時に『ゆるキャン△ つなげるみんなのオールインワン!! ちるタイム』へとフルリニューアルされる。
「ゆるキャン△」のキャンプゲーム『つなキャン△』、10月22日に“フルリニューアル”でSteamにも進出へ。その名も『ちるキャン△』
『ゆるキャン△ つなげるみんなのオールインワン!!』（通称：つなキャン△）は、TVアニメ「ゆるキャン△」を原作とするゲームだ。各務原なでしこや志摩リンなど、お馴染みのキャラクターたちがフルボイスで登場。そして目的地や参加メンバー、また持っていくキャンプギアや作るキャンプ飯などを選択し、キャンプをおこなう。

packages.headline: 「圧倒的に好評」ローグライトタワーディフェンス『Emberward』、アプデとともに正式リリース。ポータルまみれ新エリアや「マグマ射出」新タワーなどどっさり実装

sources.label: AUTOMATON
sources.evidenceText:
Refic Gamesは9月18日、『Emberward』を正式リリースした。正式リリースにあたっては、新エリア「Void Depths」や新たなタワーなどが追加されている。
「圧倒的に好評」ローグライトタワーディフェンス『Emberward』、アプデとともに正式リリース。ポータルまみれ新エリアや「マグマ射出」新タワーなどどっさり実装
デベロッパーのRefic Gamesは9月18日、『 Emberward 』を正式リリースした。対応プラットフォームはPC（Steam）で、ゲーム内は日本語表示に対応している。
『Emberward』は、ブロックを組み合わせた迷路作りと防衛戦を融合したローグライト・タワーディフェンスゲームだ。プレイヤーは監視役となり、「命の炎」を守ることになる。敵の進路を自ら組み替えながら防衛網を築き、押し寄せるモンスターを迎え撃つのだ。
『Emberward』は早期アクセス段階から好評を博しており、Steamユーザーレビューは本稿執筆時点で約3800件中96％が好評とする「圧倒的に好評」ステータスを獲得している。本作は、ブロックを組み合わせて敵の進行ルートそのものを作り変える迷路構築と、多彩なタワーを配置するタワーディフェンスを組み合わせたゲームプレイが持ち味だ。限られた形状のブロックをどう並べて敵を遠回りさせるか、そのうえでどこにどのタワーを置くかを考える必要があり、迷路作りと防衛設備の配置が密接に結びついている。こうした独自のシステムが支持を集めるなか、約2年3か月にわたってアップデートが重ねられ、今回正式リリースを迎えた。
『Emberward』はPC（ Steam ）向けに配信中。リリース記念セールとして10月2日までは定価から15％オフとなる税込1955円で購入できる。デモ版も配信中だ。
本作では、バトル開始前にL字型や直線型などのブロックをフィールドへ配置し、敵の侵攻ルートを組み替えて迷路を作る。限られたブロックを組み合わせてモンスターを遠回りさせつつ、周囲にはゴールドを消費してタワーを建設し迎撃。タワーにはサイズや属性、攻撃方法などそれぞれ異なる特徴があり、サイコロの出目がダメージになる「サイコロタワー」や、敵を追いかけて攻撃する「ドローンタワー」なども存在する。地形と手札にあわせて敵の進路を引き延ばし、タワーが攻撃しやすい防衛網を組み立てていく。

packages.headline: Astartes II, the Most Anticipated Warhammer 40,000 Animation Ever, Has a New Trailer and Confirmation of Key Details

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
Games Workshop has released a new trailer for Astartes II, the most anticipated Warhammer 40,000 animation ever.
Astartes II, the Most Anticipated Warhammer 40,000 Animation Ever, Has a New Trailer and Confirmation of Key Details
For the uninitiated, the original Astartes was created by superfan Syama Pedersen, who was subsequently brought into the fold to make the official sequel. Astartes is widely accepted as the greatest Warhammer 40,000 animation ever made, official or unofficial, with only Amazon’s excellent Space Marine 2 animation for the Secret Level anthology series competing with it in quality terms. Indeed, Astartes was so good that it inspired Saber Interactive’s hugely successful Space Marine 2 in terms of the look and feel of the Space Marines themselves.
During Games Workshop’s ‘Big Autumn Preview’ event, fans were treated to a new look at Astartes II, which confirms the appearance of Deathwatch and Terminators. As the company notes in a post on Warhammer Community , fans of Space Hulk will no doubt find a lot familiar here.
ASTARTES 2 teaser Coming December We get to follow a Deathwatch unit investigating a Space Hulk! pic.twitter.com/DgveN5yz6K
Indeed, the Space Hulk vibes come through loud and clear. We see Space Marines stomp about a dark, shadowy interior which you just know will house horrible, nightmarish things in the shadows. But the first-person shot of a corridor lit only by spotlights is the clearest sign that the much-loved tabletop game, Space Hulk, was an influence.
Also in the post, Games Workshop confirmed that Astartes II will be “significantly longer” than its predecessor, which is music to fan ears. Understandably as a single-person fan project, Astartes is on the short side.
“We knew already that this was likely to feature Deathwatch and Terminators, from the unsubtle hints dropped at the end of the LAST trailer, and now we see them, they look like they mean business,” Games Workshop said. “The imposing line of storm bolter barrels and the crackle of a power fist, combined with the ominous surroundings, are certainly giving off some strong Space Hulk vibes.

packages.headline: Call of Duty Maker Activision Says the Video Game Cheat Market Generates $8.5 Billion a Year

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
Ahead of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’s release, Activision has spoken about the “multi-billion-dollar market” behind video game cheats.
Call of Duty Maker Activision Says the Video Game Cheat Market Generates $8.5 Billion a Year
Cheating is a fact of life in pretty much all online games, but Call of Duty has a reputation for it, exacerbated by the free-to-download battle royale, Warzone. Activision, like other video game companies, faces an uphill battle against cheaters and those who make and profit from them, and generative AI has made that battle even more complex.
Now, to hammer home the point about how big a deal video game cheating is, Activision's Team Ricochet has posted a blog that breaks down the business behind it.
“Cheat sellers have built a sprawling, multi-billion-dollar marketplace of resellers, subscription services, cheat reskins, illicit accounts, spoofing tools, and organized distribution networks,” Activision said, pointing to recent analysis that suggests cheat subscriptions across just 15 games generates roughly $3.5 billion annually. Activision estimates that when you include adjacent industries such as account sales, boosting, spoofing, and other services, the broader cheating economy generates about $8.5 billion each year.
You might have seen Activision post bodycam footage of a Call of Duty cheat maker being served a cease and desist order — that’s part of the legal action the company takes here. But it’s also using “technical detection” to try to clamp down on cheat makers.
RICOCHET Anti-Cheat doesn't end when your match does. Cheat makers operate around the world. So do we. We’re taking the fight directly to cheat sellers. Last weekend during the Closed Beta, we went to Ohio to takedown Elocarry. That’s not an isolated case... pic.twitter.com/IP69qlGgDD
Activision said it’s “disrupted” more than 375 reseller operations, issued more than 80 cease-and-desist demands, and helped shut down 31 primary cheat vendors. “Cheat sellers often use marketing tactics and social posts to make their operations look stable, even when they are under significant pressure,” Activision said. “We’ve seen cheat developers use social platforms to explain months of downtime with excuses like ‘the flu,’ ‘surgery,’ or a ‘car accident’ rather than acknowledge their products were detected and no longer reliable. Those messages are part of the playbook they use to reassure customers while our systems continue disrupting their networks.”

packages.headline: Control Resonant Is Almost a Picture Perfect PC Port

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
Control Resonant is nearly a picture perfect PC port, with gorgeous visuals and stellar performance on almost every PC I've tested it on.
Control Resonant Is Almost a Picture Perfect PC Port
When the Nvidia GeForce RTX 2080 Ti first came out in 2018, I was skeptical of ray tracing and DLSS. The first few games that used the tech, like Battlefield 1 and Shadow of the Tomb Raider , had fairly lackluster ray tracing implementations that didn't look great and were just a way to nuke performance without getting much out of it. It wasn’t until Control came out in the summer of 2019 that it really started to click for me.
There was just something about the lighting solution for that game that made it look better than pretty much anything else out at the time, even if it wasn’t going for total realism. It’s no surprise then, that Control Resonant follows in the original game’s footsteps, and might just be one of the most beautiful games of the year because of it. But even with the incredible things Remedy was able to do with the visuals, Control Resonant is still one of the best optimized PC games of the year so far, and even runs reasonably well on the Xbox Ally X.
Control Resonant, though, dials back on some of the ultra-realism of Alan Wake 2, and is able to scale much better to less powerful hardware. While the game definitely rewards high-end PCs with a stunning implementation of path tracing that really accentuates the game’s art style, it’s somehow even more impressive how good the game looks on a handheld.
Control Resonant does make the Steam Deck show its age a bit, though. Even with the handheld preset, set to 720p and FSR set to balanced, Valve's 4-and-a-half-year-old handheld struggles to stay above 25 fps. You can absolutely play the game like that if you want, but I wouldn't really recommend it.
I installed an RTX 4070 Ti Super and set the game to 1440p with the medium preset with ray tracing at medium, along with DLSS set to balanced. At those settings, Control Resonant averaged 111 fps, with a 1% low of 81 fps – far above Remedy's quoted 60 fps for those settings. Granted, I did test with an RTX 4070 Ti Super, which is around 10-15% faster than the recommended 4070 Ti. But even if you lopped off 15% of the frames there, it would still average 94 fps, which is better than Remedy's official system requirements suggest.
With frame generation enabled, the RTX 4070 Ti's frame rate jumps to 118 fps, although the pre-frame-gen number drops down to 60. Still, that is more than enough for Control Resonant to feel responsive, while also delivering an incredibly smooth frame rate for a high-refresh gaming monitor . Usually, turning on frame gen would come with more latency than having it off, but for some reason, Remedy doesn't include the option to turn on Nvidia reflex indepently from frame interpolation, so you actually end up with less latency with it enabled.
With how good the lighting is in Control Resonant, I probably would have come away happy if the game ran a lot worse than it does. The fact that it scales so well while looking as good as it does makes it one of the best PC ports of the year so far. If you have a halfway decent gaming PC lying around and you're planning on playing Resonant anyways, I'd recommend picking it up on Steam in a heartbeat.
Now this is what I call optimization.
Remedy’s last game was certainly a technical masterpiece as well. Alan Wake 2 is still one of the most beautiful games I’ve ever seen, and there are parts of that game that look like I’m playing through a movie, especially on higher graphics settings. But at the same time, it’s not a game that’s known for running on less powerful PCs.

packages.headline: EA Sports FC 27 Review So Far

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
EA Sports stands on shaky ground with a new open-world hub, but the realistic, intuitive Tactics system shows promise.
I find myself in a weird place for my in-progress review of EA Sports FC 27. On one hand, worthwhile strategic elements have finally been added that reflect real-world tactics in a concise, intuitive way. On the other hand, the promised improvements to behavior and pathing of computer-controlled players on the field still ring hollow, carrying over many of the same issues the series has had for over a decade. Couple this with the dreaded introduction of open-world elements via The Grounds, and the result is yet another instance of positive steps forward but negative steps backward.
Ever since NBA 2K14 introduced MyPark, which eventually evolved into The Neighborhood in NBA 2K18 and The City in NBA 2K21, I figured it was only a matter of time before EA brought a similar open world full of activities to its sports franchises. While The Grounds isn't without merit, it often feels like EA is trying to solve a problem that didn't really exist.
My first impression is that The Grounds doesn’t need to be an open-world environment to deliver what the playerbase wants out of a more communal online mode. I don’t need to run through a visually saturated, low-resolution city populated by lifeless NPCs just to find a game mode to start up when simple menus devoted to the same function can do the same thing in a more efficient manner. Sure, it works well as an active lobby for matchmaking and makes it easier to find other players and move between activities, but between the framerate drops and unnatural character animations, nothing immersed me in the hub in EA Sports FC 27 enough to justify its existence.
When it comes to gameplay, EA Sports FC 27's expanded Tactics system is easily the best addition, wonderfully complementing the playstyles and roles introduced over the past few years. The new strategy system gives much more control over how teams behave in different phases of play, going beyond basic formations and instructions by explaining the purpose, strengths, and weaknesses of different tactical approaches. This becomes particularly useful when building around individual player attributes. As a Manchester United fan, I found that a deeper defensive approach worked especially well for Noussair Mazraoui, whose patient style lets him maintain his position and disrupt attacks without constantly stepping out of shape, while a short-passing buildup gives him chances to use his technical ability without abandoning that defensive structure.
Read the full EA Sports FC 26 review .
That same flexibility can be useful defensively, particularly when protecting a lead. If an opponent repeatedly targets his side of the pitch, giving Šeško more defensive responsibility lets him drop back and support the right back, providing another way to protect that flank without abandoning the attacking structure. What makes the system particularly valuable is that it teaches the strategy behind soccer formations without overwhelming players with unnecessary information. EA Sports FC 27 does a good job explaining why different shapes work, which players suit them, and how to adjust them against different opponents, making the tactical aspect for the sport approachable while still leaving experienced players plenty of room to experiment.
Crossing and corner kicks have also improved noticeably, with both systems producing more convincing positioning battles and giving the player greater control over what happens inside the box. I scored several successful headers with Harry Maguire from corners during my time with the game, which stood out because I could count on one hand the number of corner routines and headed goals I had scored in previous EA Sports FC entries.

packages.headline: IGN 30 Anniversary Bundle Is Live: Get 7 PC Games for $15

sources.evidenceText:
IGN is 30, and to celebrate, we've teamed up with Humble to offer a bundle of 7 excellent PC games for just $15.
IGN 30 Anniversary Bundle Is Live: Get 7 PC Games for $15
Did you know that this very website is now 30 years old? Look at the logo at the top of this page if you don't believe me. To celebrate, the IGN 30 Anniversary Bundle is now live, which getes you seven Steam PC games for just $15 on Humble. The games are all worth checking out, and genre-wise there’s a little something for everyone. There’s an MMO, a Souls-like shooter, a survival game, and more. Let’s dive in.

Thronebreaker: The Witcher Tales got a 9.4/10 review that same year, with our critic calling it, “one of the best-written RPGs I’ve played in years.”

Remnant 2, Elder Scrolls Online: Elsweyr, and more.

packages.headline: Marvel's Wolverine Has 'Sold Well,' Early Data Suggests, but Don't Expect Spider-Man Numbers

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
Sony has yet to announce an official sales figure for Marvel’s Wolverine, but one analyst has said early data suggests it's sold 1.9 million copies since going on sale on September 15, generating around $130 million in revenue.
Marvel's Wolverine Has 'Sold Well,' Early Data Suggests, but Don't Expect Spider-Man Numbers
Sony has yet to announce an official sales figure for Marvel’s Wolverine , but one analyst has said early data suggests it's sold 1.9 million copies since going on sale on September 15, generating around $130 million in revenue.
Through all this, it’s important to note that Sony has yet to make any official sales announcement for Marvel’s Wolverine. It has made sales announcements for PlayStation Studios games in the past. For example, Sucker Punch’s Ghost of Yotei went on sale on October 2, 2025 and sold 3.3 million units as of November 2 (at the 32 day mark), according to Sony’s official figures.
Back in October 23, Sony announced that Insomniac's PlayStation 5 exclusive Spider-Man 2 sold more than 2.5 million copies in 24 hours , which meant the open-world superhero game overtook Santa Monica Studio’s God of War Ragnarok at the top of the PlayStation day-one launch sales chart. At the time, it was the fastest-selling PlayStation Studios game in history (Helldivers 2 now holds top spot).
Assuming Alinea Analytics is in the right ballpark, Marvel’s Wolverine is tracking behind Spider-Man 2. But it has already passed the lifetime PS5 copies sold and revenues of Hideo Kojima’s Death Stranding 2, which hit the headlines when Sony ditched Kojima’s Physint. Indeed, according to Elliot, Marvel’s Wolverine is after just a few days on sale the top-performing new PlayStation Studios game released on PS5 so far this year, ahead of MLB The Show, Bungie’s Marathon, Housemarque’s Saros, and fighting game Marvel Tōkon.
The big question is how well Wolverine continues to sell. Wolverine is currently sitting on a 77 Metascore , with IGN’s Marvel’s Wolverine review returning a 6/10. We said: “Marvel's Wolverine's slick and satisfying combat wears thin well before its conclusion, so much so that even its strong character work can't quite save it from being anything more than okay.”
“So yes, Wolverine has sold well, but its commercial long tail is limited by its mixed media and streamer reception,” Elliott said. “Unlike Spider-Man, which reviewed insanely well and has stayed evergreen for years, this one’s tail will be shorter and lumpier, but still there.”
Expect a bump when the MCU kicks into gear this December with the release of Avengers: Doomsday, which features the X-Men (but does it feature Hugh Jackman’s Wolverine?). Wolverine might also benefit from the expanded PS5 install base that will inevitably kick in with the release of GTA 6 in November. And Wolverine is sure to prove a popular choice under the Christmas tree.
Rhys Elliott, head of market analysis at Alinea Analytics, took to social media to say an estimated 22.9% of that revenue came from the sale of physical copies of the game — remember, Sony plans to cease production of PlayStation discs from 2028.
